task.prompt: Write the recommendation summary of a business case for the client's leadership, based on the context.
task.context: Client: online furniture retailer. Problem: 18,000 support tickets a month, 40% about order status. Options: (A) do nothing; (B) self-service order tracking page: $35k build, deflects about 25% of tickets; (C) AI support assistant with order lookup: $110k build plus $36k/year running costs, deflects about 45% of tickets in pilots elsewhere, accuracy risk on returns policy. Cost per ticket handled by an agent: $4.

rubric.label: Clear recommendation
rubric.description: Names the recommended option and why in the first lines.

rubric.label: Uses the numbers
rubric.description: Compares options with figures derived from the context, e.g. tickets deflected and annual savings.

rubric.label: States risks and assumptions
rubric.description: Notes the AI accuracy risk, the pilot-based estimate, and how they will be managed or tested.

rubric.label: Next step
rubric.description: Proposes a decision or a staged next step such as a pilot with success criteria.

task.sampleAnswer:
Recommendation: build the order-tracking page now (Option B) and run a 3-month pilot of the AI assistant (Option C) before committing to a full rollout.

Why: Option B deflects about 4,500 tickets a month (25% of 18,000), saving about $18,000 a month ($216k a year) for $35k. It pays back in about two months with low risk.

Option C could deflect about 8,100 tickets a month (45%), saving roughly $389k a year against $110k build and $36k a year running cost. However, the 45% comes from other companies' pilots, and errors on returns policy could create complaints and refunds.

Assumptions: $4 per ticket; deflection rates as stated; Option C's savings overlap with B's on order status.

Next step: approve B now; approve a pilot of C limited to order status, with success criteria of 35% deflection and under 2% escalations from wrong answers, before deciding on full rollout.

segments.text: Baseline: current handling time 9.5 minutes per ticket, from 3 months of data.

segments.issue: A long period inflates ROI; state a realistic horizon given model and platform change.

segments.text: Benefit owner: head of customer support.
The case will be reviewed at each phase gate.
Risks: model accuracy, data-protection review, user adoption.

prompt: Why include a do-nothing option in a business case?

options: It is the baseline every other option must beat
It makes the recommendation look better
mcq.explanation: Without the cost of inaction, there is nothing to compare benefits against.

prompt: What is the main weakness of payback period as a measure?

options: It ignores benefits after payback and the time value of money
mcq.explanation: Two projects with the same payback can differ hugely afterwards; use NPV too.

prompt: A positive NPV at the company's cost of capital means:

options: The project will pay back in a year
The investment is expected to earn more than the alternative use of that money
Benefits exceed costs before discounting only
mcq.explanation: NPV above zero means the discounted benefits exceed the discounted costs.
